take_homes: An agent's review of its own work is too kind, so someone independent has to check it. This is a real control point.
The agent fills gaps with plausible filler, so a gap should be flagged. I should not accept an invented answer.
What you teach it can be saved in a rules file and reused, so a task like the month-end commentary could be repeated by a fresh agent.

monday.move: Ask my controller whether the month-end variance commentary could be drafted by an agent from last month's actual file, with the controller checking every figure. I would ask IT first whether the tool can touch finance data.
monday.who: Controller, plus IT for the approval
monday.stop_condition: The controller spends more time checking the draft than writing it, or one figure is wrong and nobody caught it
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data. No cost per user per month was given.

misconception.why: Nothing said what this costs or what the organisation has to build around the licence. The rules file and the independent check hint at capability, but I got there by inference. Nobody said so.

one_line: There are two or three ideas worth having, mainly don't trust the agent's self-review and don't fill gaps with plausible answers. But it's buried in repeated filler, a personal website exercise, and not a single figure on cost or payback.
